title: per-path-sampling-and-staged-latency-attribution-for-long-tail-prompts
author: Leah Park
release_notes: Adds path-aware sampling and staged latency attribution metrics; new dashboards and tuned alerts for long-tail prompt behavior; minor SDK trace header change; rollout requires a two-phase trace agent upgrade.
description:
Context and motivation:
The production alert noise and tail-latency incidents over the last quarter are dominated by a small number of rarely-exercised request paths and long-tail prompts. Existing rollups and uniform sampling mask path-specific regressions and lead to broad, noisy paging. This PR introduces a lightweight, path-aware sampling layer plus a staged latency attribution pipeline so we can: 1) reliably surface regressions tied to request path or prompt family, 2) attribute latency across pipeline stages (network, tokenization, embedding, KV-cache, model compute) for faster root cause, and 3) lower alert noise by switching to path-specific baselines and delta detection.

What this implements:
- Adaptive path-aware reservoir sampling: per-path hashed reservoir with age-based decay and priority uplift for low-frequency keys. Sampling keys are request path + prompt fingerprint. The sampler exports sampling_rate_by_path metric and attaches a sampling.trace_header so traces for sampled requests are routed into the new staged attribution pipeline.
- Staged latency attribution service (telemetry/attribution): aligns trace span timestamps and computes stage-level latency per request (network, tokenize, embed, kv_cache_wait, model_infer). Emits path.staged_latency.{p50,p95} and path.token_cost_estimate metrics and a path.latency.change detector signal. Attribution is deterministic for sampled traces and produces a synthetic replay hook for high-fidelity investigations.
- Telemetry and dashboards: new Grafana dashboard (dashboards/long_tail_path_attribution.json) with per-path heatmap, stacked stage breakdown, and a side-by-side token-cost histogram. Added per-path anomaly panel that uses the new change detector signal.
- Alert tuning: replaces a global p95 alert for inference latency with per-path adaptive SLO alert rules (alerts/path-p95-adaptive.yaml). Alerts now use a rolling baseline computed from path-specific historical percentiles and trigger only on statistically significant deviations.
- SDK trace header update: small addition to Python/TS SDKs to propagate the sampling.trace_header when present; backward compatible when header missing.
- Instrumentation: lightweight cgroup-friendly timers in runtime to capture tokenize/embed/kv waits without adding CPU overhead; sampling off by default for high-cardinality paths.

Checklist (what I ran locally / in staging):
- [x] Unit tests for sampler and attribution logic
- [x] Integration test in telemetry stack with local jaeger + metrics sink
- [x] Canary: deployed to canary cluster for 48h; validated sampled traces and metrics match expected stage boundaries
- [x] Load test: 1k rps synthetic workload with 10% long-tail paths to measure overhead (observed ~0.8% median CPU increase, <2% P95)
- [x] Dashboard panels reviewed with Observability SRE and UX tweaks applied
- [x] Alerting rules staged in staging alert manager and evaluated against historical data

Review conversation highlights:
- Maya Chen (reviewer): "Overall this looks solid and addresses a big source of noise. My main concern is sampling cost and cardinality explosion — can we guarantee explicit opt-out for any path via config? Also please quantify metric cardinality limits for the metrics backend."
- Leah Park (author): "Answer: sampler respects a default deny list by config and exposes sampling_rate_by_path metric so SRE can automatically detect high-cardinality paths. Added docs/observability/long-tail-paths.md with operational guidance and a config knob 'telemetry.path_sampler.max_distinct_keys' (default 5000)."
- Sanjay Rao (reviewer): "Attribution logic looks good; request one change — prefer renaming 'kv_cache_wait' -> 'kv_wait' for naming consistency across other dashboards."
- Leah Park: "Renamed span label to kv_wait and updated dashboards and tests."
- Diego Alvarez (approver): "Load impact acceptable in canary. Approving after CI passes and minor lint fix."

CI summary:
- Initial run: lint failed (trailing whitespace, one exported symbol missing docstring) — fixed in a8e3f5b
- Unit tests: pass
- Integration tests: pass
- Load test job: pass (see artifacts/load-tests/2026-01-30)

Migration and rollout notes:
- Two-phase rollout required: 1) Deploy telemetry agents and attribution service to canary and collect sampling_rate_by_path for 48h; 2) Enable sampling for low-volume paths incrementally and switch alerting rules on via feature flag 'telemetry.path_sampling.enabled'.
- SDKs: rolling upgrade of SDKs recommended for customers that rely on trace header propagation. Backward compatibility preserved; missing headers are treated as unsampled.
- Dashboard owners: Observability SRE and Infra dashboards team to review panels post-merge and tune any path-specific thresholds.

Risks and mitigations:
- Cardinality explosion: mitigated via max_distinct_keys config, default denylist, and sampled traces only. Metrics aggregator has a tag cardinality cap; we intentionally expose a small set of path-level metrics (p50/p95 and change signal) rather than full histogram per path unless enabled.
- CPU overhead: measured during load test as <2% P95 CPU; attribution work is asynchronous and bounded by a token-limited worker pool.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Auto-cohorting: group similar prompts by embedding similarity to reduce path cardinality and enable cohort-level SLOs (ENG-5112)
- Automated remediation: integrate with rollout system to auto-fallback model variants on path-specific regressions

Merge outcome:
- Merged to main via squash by Diego Alvarez on 2026-02-11 after final CI green and canary acceptance.

If you want to run through the canary artifacts or replay a sampled trace, see the two scripts in scripts/load-tests and the synthetic replayer in telemetry/attribution/replayer (note: replayer is gated behind canary flag).
notes: Kept sampling disabled for high-cardinality traffic by default; docs include runbook for SREs to escalate if new high-cardinality paths appear.
